FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.85
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_manager.py` apply_diagnosis (lines 1253–1320) and `_immune.py` record_model_round (lines 619, 655, 724). Three pathology types — `parser_yield`, `monotonic_decline`, and `cpf_spike` — have remediation chains defined in `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS` (lines 1006–1041) but are unreachable from apply_diagnosis. The pathology_key emitted by DetectorHealthMonitor includes the model_id suffix (e.g. `parser_yield_modelX`, `monotonic_decline_modelX`, `cpf_spike_modelX`). apply_diagnosis first checks `diagnosis.pathology_key in self._REMEDIATION_CHAINS` — this fails because the chain keys are the generic forms (`parser_yield`, `monotonic_decline`, `cpf_spike`). The fallback elif chain (lines 1256–1263) only handles `kappa`, `vocab_saturation`, `findings_decline`, and `model_failure` by detector name; there are no branches for detector=`parser_yield`, detector=`monotonic_decline`, or detector=`cpf_spike`. chain_key remains None, and apply_diagnosis returns None at line 1320. FOLLOW: These three pathology types are detected, logged, emitted as events, and then discarded without remediation. The entire chain definitions for them are dead code. This spans DetectorHealthMonitor (detection), DynamicManager (routing), and _REMEDIATION_CHAINS (specification) — three subsystems that believe they are connected but are not.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add elif branches in apply_diagnosis for the three missing detector types, stripping the model_id suffix to derive the generic chain_key. For example: `elif diagnosis.detector == "parser_yield": chain_key = "parser_yield"`, and similarly for `monotonic_decline` and `cpf_spike`. Alternatively, emit pathology_keys without the model_id suffix (using the evidence dict to carry the model_id) to match the chain key directly.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_immune.py` _CHAIN_TO_COUNTER mapping (lines 1016–1022) maps only 5 of the 11 chain keys to their corresponding _pathology_counts keys. Missing: `model_failure`, `parser_yield`, `monotonic_decline`, `cpf_spike`, `dispatch_false_positive`, `verification_miscalibration`. FOLLOW: When _verify_remediation_outcomes succeeds for a per-model chain (line 836: `self._pathology_counts.pop(self._CHAIN_TO_COUNTER.get(pathology_key, pathology_key), None)`), the fallback is the chain_key itself (e.g. `model_failure`), but _pathology_counts uses `model_failure_{model_id}`. The pop silently misses. Consequence: the pathology counter never resets on successful remediation, so persistence escalation (WARNING→CRITICAL) ratchets up permanently and the adaptive sensitivity window keeps narrowing based on stale counts. Same stale-counter problem occurs on chain exhaustion (line 861). This crosses the health monitor (counters), the orchestrator (chain routing), and the remediation verification loop (cleanup).
PROPOSED_FIX: Either (a) extend _CHAIN_TO_COUNTER with entries for all per-model chain keys and make the pop use the actual per-model counter key derived from `diagnosis.evidence["model_id"]`, or (b) change _verify_remediation_outcomes to pass the original detector-scoped counter key through the remediation state dict so the pop targets the correct key.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_failure_handler.py` reset_round_state() (line 382) clears _realloc_depth to prevent permanent reallocation blocking (FH-7 fix). However, `_manager.py` process_round() never calls `self.failure_handler.reset_round_state()`. Grep confirms zero call sites in _manager.py. FOLLOW: Once any task hits max_realloc_depth (default 2), check_reallocation_depth returns False for that task_id permanently. Since _realloc_depth is a dict keyed by task_id and tasks may be reused across rounds, this is equivalent to the pre-FH-7 bug: the fix exists but the orchestrator never invokes it. The method is dead code in the current call graph. This crosses FailureHandler (provides reset), process_round (orchestration), and the cascade guard logic (consumers of the depth check).
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `self.failure_handler.reset_round_state()` at the beginning of process_round(), before the failure detection loop. This is where round-boundary state resets belong.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_failure_handler.py` detect_failure (lines 173–180). When a FORMAT failure is detected, the emitted ManagerEvent uses `event_type=ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` (line 175), not `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. FOLLOW: Downstream consumers — the PM event callback, ManagerEventStream, and any event-based monitoring — cannot distinguish FORMAT from MALFORMED failures by event type alone. Both appear as MALFORMED. The ManagerEventType enum defines a distinct `FORMAT_VIOLATION` value (line 567) which exists precisely for this purpose but is never used. This affects the cross-subsystem contract between FailureHandler (emitter), the event stream (transport), and any external consumer (PM, logging, metrics dashboards). A PM monitoring for FORMAT-specific patterns will never see them.
PROPOSED_FIX: Change line 175 from `event_type=ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` to `event_type=ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.79
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_manager.py` line 630: `self._regression_defer = True`. This flag is a one-way latch — once set, it is never reset to False anywhere in the codebase. FOLLOW: After a single regression detection (finding_count drops >30% within 2 rounds of a fix), all future autonomous immune remediation is permanently disabled for the rest of the session. apply_diagnosis checks this flag at line 1236 and returns None. There is no recovery path: even if the regression was transient, even if subsequent metrics fully recover, even if the regressed fix was for a different pathology than the one currently detected. The immune layer is permanently lobotomised after one bad fix. This interacts across regression detection (process_round lines 594–635), apply_diagnosis (line 1236), and every pathology detection path that feeds into apply_diagnosis.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either (a) reset `_regression_defer` after N rounds of healthy metrics (e.g. finding_count recovers to pre-regression levels for resolution_hysteresis consecutive rounds), or (b) make `_regression_defer` per-chain-key rather than global, so a regression in one pathology doesn't block remediation of unrelated pathologies.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.77
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_failure_handler.py` detect_failure (lines 183–206). The UNDERPERFORM check is the only failure type that does not emit a ManagerEvent via _emit_event(). EMPTY (line 136), TIMEOUT (line 149), MALFORMED (line 161), and FORMAT (line 173) all emit events before returning. UNDERPERFORM silently returns the failure type with no event. FOLLOW: The PM callback never receives real-time notification of underperformance. The event stream's record of failure events has a systematic gap for one of five failure types. Any monitoring, alerting, or analysis that depends on the event stream (including the ManagerEventStream wired at DynamicManager.__init__ line 216) will undercount failures. The ManagerEventType enum defines an `UNDERPERFORM` event type (line 568) that is never emitted by FailureHandler.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an `_emit_event()` call in the UNDERPERFORM detection branch (between lines 205 and 206) emitting a `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` event with the performance metric details as evidence.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_manager.py` set_remediation_state call at line 1472–1478 does not pass `chain_length=len(chain)`. The `set_remediation_state` signature (in `_immune.py` line 731) defaults `chain_length` to 999. FOLLOW: The RV-1 bounds check in `_verify_remediation_outcomes` (line 854: `if next_idx >= chain_len`) uses `state.get("chain_length", 999)`. Since the actual chain length is never passed, the bounds check is effectively disabled — escalation can increment chain_idx up to 999 before hitting the cap, long past the actual end of any chain (the longest chain has 3 steps). This means for chains shorter than 999, the escalation will attempt to index past the chain list, hitting the `chain_idx >= len(chain)` check in apply_diagnosis (line 1353) instead. The redundant safety net catches it, but the RV-1 fix in _verify_remediation_outcomes is dead: it can never trigger because 999 >> any chain length. The intended fail-fast path (exhaustion detected at verification time) never fires.
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass `chain_length=len(chain)` in the `set_remediation_state` call at line 1472. This enables the RV-1 bounds check to fire at verification time rather than deferring to the apply_diagnosis fallback.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F008
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_manager.py` line 374: `if not hasattr(self, '_process_round_count'): self._process_round_count = 0`. This lazily initializes round tracking outside __init__. FOLLOW: If any code path reads `self._process_round_count` before the first process_round call (e.g. approve_deferred_remediation at line 1502: `getattr(self, '_process_round_count', 0)`), it silently defaults to 0 via getattr. The more consequential issue is that `_process_round_count` can diverge from the FSM's round index if process_round is called with retry semantics after a failure, or if the FSM has been manually advanced. The round_idx used for all immune operations (failure recording, convergence feeding, remediation state) comes from this counter, while the FSM maintains its own independent counter. There is no synchronisation check between them.
PROPOSED_FIX: Move `self._process_round_count = 0` into __init__ alongside the other state initialisations. Add an assertion or warning if `_process_round_count != self.fsm.current_round` at entry to detect divergence.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F009
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_manager.py` apply_diagnosis (lines 1096–1107, 1146–1158, 1170–1183, 1300–1309) and _apply_transform (lines 1096–1183). Multiple directive-injection transforms (`add_synthesis_directive`, `add_parsing_directive`, `add_verification_directive`, and the verification_miscalibration handler) check `model_id not in self.config.per_model_directives` before writing. This means if a model already has ANY directive (from registry loading, a prior immune fix, or a different pathology), the new directive is silently dropped. FOLLOW: Directives are not composable — a model that received a parsing directive in round 2 cannot also receive a synthesis directive in round 4. The first pathology to inject a directive wins; all subsequent pathology-specific directives for that model are permanently blocked. There is no append, merge, or replacement logic. This crosses the registry loader (Phase A), all immune directive transforms, and the per-model dispatch path that consumes these directives.
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the guard from "not in" to an append/concatenation with length enforcement: `existing = self.config.per_model_directives.get(model_id, ""); combined = existing + " " + directive; if len(combined) <= self.config.max_per_model_directive_chars: self.config.per_model_directives[model_id] = combined`. This allows directive composition within the character budget.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CC_IM_F010
SEVERITY: 0.68
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_immune.py` _standard_p_pass_remediation Check 2 (lines 1129–1158). The "already improving" veto checks whether the target metric has been non-declining for 3 consecutive rounds. For most metrics, the test is `recent_3[i] >= recent_3[i - 1] * 0.95`. When a metric is negative (mu can be negative as indicated by the abs() handling elsewhere), this comparison inverts: -0.5 >= -0.6 * 0.95 = -0.57 is true, so a metric that is getting MORE negative (worse) is classified as "improving". The mu-specific branch uses abs() comparisons, but the general branch does not, and `finding_count` is always non-negative so it's safe there. However, if any future metric can be negative and uses the default branch, the veto fires incorrectly. More immediately, the `vocab_growth` metric could in principle be 0.0 throughout (no growth), and 0.0 >= 0.0 * 0.95 = True, causing the P-pass to permanently veto all vocab_saturation remediations even when the metric is flatlined at zero — which is precisely the pathology being remediated. The flatline-at-zero guard (line 1137) catches the all-zero case but not the case where values are very small non-zero (e.g. 0.001, 0.001, 0.002).
PROPOSED_FIX: For the vocab_growth check, compare against the tau_vocab_growth threshold rather than trend direction — if current_val < tau_vg, the metric is still pathological regardless of whether it's "improving". Mirror the direction-aware logic from _verify_remediation_outcomes (line 801–803) which already handles this correctly for vocab_growth.
VERIFIED: TRUE
